subject.title: Feature: Distinguish webchat client types (Mac app vs browser)

question: Which WebChat client metadata may agents see, and should it come only from authenticated Gateway connect identity or also from caller-supplied browser/app hints?
rationale: The requested metadata can affect agent behavior and potentially capability selection, so the trust boundary and semantics need maintainer intent before implementation.

options.title: Expose trusted connect identity only
options.body: Expose normalized Gateway client id, mode, and platform from the authenticated connection as read-only runtime metadata, and reject ad hoc chat/header claims for policy.

options.title: Keep identity diagnostic-only
options.body: Keep client id, mode, and platform in Gateway logs and presence without exposing it to agents until there is a stronger product requirement.

options.title: Allow explicit caller hints
options.body: Add a client-supplied metadata field or header documented as untrusted and excluded from security or policy decisions.

recommendation.title: Expose trusted connect identity only
recommendation.body: Expose normalized Gateway client id, mode, and platform from the authenticated connection as read-only runtime metadata, and reject ad hoc chat/header claims for policy.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is a Gateway/WebChat trust-boundary decision, and recent history places this handle closest to Gateway auth/security work.
